items.bold: TRUMP ordered US Navy "SHOOT AND KILL" Iranian mine-laying boats in Hormuz.
items.text: PBS, NPR, CBC, AP and CNBC confirmed: Trump posted Thursday: "I have ordered the United States Navy to shoot and kill any boat, small boats though they may be...that is putting mines in the waters of the Strait of Hormuz. There is to be no hesitation. Additionally, our mine sweepers are clearing the Strait right now. I am hereby ordering that activity to continue, but at a tripled up level!" Trump also claimed: "We have total control over the Strait of Hormuz. No ship can enter or leave without the approval of the United States Navy. It is sealed up tight until such time as Iran is able to make a deal." The IRGC called the shoot-to-kill order "an overt breach of the ceasefire." PBS reported the NYT separately cited US officials saying mine-clearing could take up to six months. This is the most aggressive US Rules of Engagement change since the war began February 28.

items.bold: ISRAEL-LEBANON CEASEFIRE EXTENDED 3 WEEKS — White House Thursday. One deadline removed.
items.text: WaPo, NPR, CNBC, and CBS News confirmed: Trump announced Thursday evening that the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire was extended by three weeks after a meeting in the White House Oval Office. Trump posted on Truth Social: "The Ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon will be extended by THREE WEEKS. The Meeting went very well!" Secretary of State Rubio and State Department Counselor Michael Needham led the talks; Israel and Lebanon were represented by their ambassadors to the US. Trump said the US would "work with Lebanon in order to help it protect itself from Hezbollah." This removes the Lebanon ceasefire expiry as a converging deadline — the most dangerous scenario was Iran using a Lebanon collapse as a pretext for Hormuz escalation simultaneously with the Trump Iran deadline. That risk is now deferred by three weeks. The remaining active deadline is Trump's 3-5 day window for Iran (~April 25-27).

items.bold: ISRAEL DEFENSE MINISTER KATZ: Ready to resume war with Iran — awaiting US green light.
items.text: CBC News and CBS News confirmed: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz stated Thursday that Israel is "prepared to resume war with Iran" and is awaiting a "green light" from the United States. Katz said the military is "ready for both defensive and offensive operations and targets are marked." This is the most explicit Israeli military readiness statement since the ceasefire began April 8. Combined with the 50,000+ US troops in the region and Trump's shoot-to-kill order for mine-laying boats, the West Asia War is closer to resuming than at any point since the ceasefire. Katz's statement is also significant because it signals Israel and the US are coordinating closely on the timing of any resumed strikes — it will not be unilateral.

items.bold: THIRD US TANKER BOARDED overnight — ex-Phonix (Indian Ocean). 31 ships total turned back.
items.text: PBS and Time confirmed: US forces boarded another sanctioned tanker overnight Thursday in the Indian Ocean — the vessel previously named "Phonix," sanctioned by US Treasury in 2024 for smuggling Iranian crude oil. This is the third ship boarding in the Indian Ocean region (after Tifani April 21). CENTCOM stated: "We will continue global maritime enforcement to disrupt illicit networks and interdict vessels providing material support to Iran, wherever they operate." CENTCOM separately confirmed 31 vessels total have been directed to turn around or return to port since the blockade began April 13 — up from 28. The shadow fleet enforcement is extending to the Indo-Pacific. India's maritime neighbourhood is directly affected.

items.bold: PHILIPPINES: 15 Filipino seafarers on IRGC-seized ships — safe. India: 280 in zone.
items.text: CBS News confirmed the Philippine government confirmed 15 Filipino seafarers were aboard the seized Hormuz vessels — 10 on the Epaminondas and 5 on the MSC Francesca. Philippine Department of Migrant Workers said they are "safe and unharmed." Iran's state media released dramatically-edited video Thursday of IRGC forces in black masks boarding the MSC Francesca — masked fighters speeding toward the ship in a gunboat, climbing ladders up the hull with rifles slung over backs. CBS confirmed the video. For India: 280 Indian seafarers remain in the broader Gulf zone across 8 vessels. MEA channel with Tehran active. Op Urja Suraksha warships on HIGH ALERT. The third Indian Ocean tanker boarding overnight adds risk to India-adjacent sea lanes.

items.bold: US NAVY SECRETARY PHELAN FIRED — acting: Hung Cao. Dept loses top civilian during active blockade.
items.text: CBS News and Time confirmed: Navy Secretary John Phelan was dismissed — chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell confirmed "effective immediately." Undersecretary of the Navy Hung Cao named acting civilian lead. Cao is a Navy veteran who ran as the GOP's Senate nominee in Virginia in 2024, losing to Democratic Sen. Tim Kaine. Trump said Phelan "did an outstanding job" and would "like to have him back in the Trump Administration." The dismissal comes as the US Navy is actively enforcing the Hormuz blockade, conducting three ship boardings, operating minesweepers, and now under new orders to shoot mine-laying boats on sight. Losing the top civilian official at this critical moment is operationally significant — the acting lead has no Senate confirmation.

assessment.headline: DAY 56, 9:30 AM FRI: TRUMP ordered SHOOT AND KILL for Iranian mine-laying boats. ISRAEL ready to resume war. Lebanon ceasefire EXTENDED 3 WEEKS. Brent $106+. GIFT Nifty +69. Infosys +21% beat opening today. Iran ~Apr 25-27 deadline remains. Mine clearing: 6 months.
assessment.body:
Friday 9:30 AM IST. Markets opening positive despite the most aggressive US military order since the war began.

THE SHOOT-TO-KILL ORDER
• Trump posted Thursday: ordered Navy to "shoot and kill" Iranian mine-laying boats
• "There is to be no hesitation"
• Mine sweepers ordered to triple operations
• IRGC: order is "overt breach of ceasefire"
• Mine clearing could take up to 6 months (NYT/US officials via PBS)
• Even a deal today = Hormuz restricted for months during clearing

ISRAEL READY TO RESUME WAR
• Defense Minister Katz: "prepared to resume war with Iran"
• Awaiting "green light" from the United States
• "Targets are marked" — both defensive and offensive operations ready
• This is the most explicit Israeli readiness statement since April 8 ceasefire

THE POSITIVE OFFSET — LEBANON CEASEFIRE EXTENDED
• White House Thursday: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire extended by THREE WEEKS
• Trump+Vance+Rubio+Needham in Oval Office — ambassadors of Israel and Lebanon present
• Removes Lebanon expiry from the April 25-27 dual deadline risk
• The most dangerous scenario (Lebanon collapse + Iran deadline simultaneously) is deferred

REMAINING RISK: IRAN 3-5 DAY DEADLINE
• Trump gave Iran 3-5 days from April 22 = ~April 25-27
• No unified proposal received from Iran yet
• Ghalibaf adviser: ceasefire extension "means nothing"
• IRGC: shoot-to-kill order is "overt ceasefire breach"
• Iran has 48 hours to submit proposal or deadline expires

INDIA OPENING TODAY
• GIFT Nifty +69 at 24,232 = positive open
• Infosys Q4 PAT +21% beat (announced after hours Thursday) — NOT yet priced in
• IT sector recovery expected — two days of underperformance reversing
• Brent $106 = OMC petrol/diesel hike within 1-2 days — now near-certain
• Rupee ~95.00 — weakening on $106 Brent
• Lebanon extension removes tail risk → partially risk-on

STRUCTURAL HORMUZ FACTS
• Mine clearing: up to 6 months even with a deal (NYT/PBS)
• Third US tanker boarded Indian Ocean overnight (ex-Phonix)
• 31 ships total turned back since April 13 blockade
• 15 Filipino crew on seized ships (safe)
• 280 Indian seafarers still in Gulf zone
• Navy Sec Phelan fired — acting: Hung Cao (no Senate confirmation)

VERDICT: Friday opens with the West Asia War at its most militarily escalated point since the ceasefire. Trump has authorised lethal force on Iranian vessels. Israel has its finger on the trigger. Brent is at $106. Yet GIFT Nifty is positive — markets are choosing to focus on the Lebanon ceasefire extension and the Infosys beat. The next 48-72 hours will determine whether Iran's deadline produces a proposal or the shoot-to-kill order produces an incident that forces both sides back to full war.
